question.prompt:
All six sides of a rectangular solid were rectangles. A one-foot cube was cut out of the rectangular solid as shown. The total number of square feet in the surface of the new solid is how many more or less than that of the original solid?

[Figure 1](figures/1991_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Only the surfaces next to the cut can change, so we can compare those without finding the whole surface area.

[Figure 1](figures/1991_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

The solid is \(1\) foot thick, so the one-foot cube is cut all the way from the front to the back. The cut removes a \(1\)-foot square from each of the top, front, and back surfaces. Thus \(3\) square feet of the original surface disappear.

The cut also exposes three new squares: the floor of the notch and its two side walls. Each has area \(1\times1=1\) square foot, so \(3\) square feet are added. Every other surface stays unchanged. Therefore the change is
\[
3-3=0\text{ square feet}.
\]
The surface area is the same, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the surfaces removed and exposed
